lessons.name: MalocherBot
lessons.summary: MalocherBot is a modular industrial automation cell that combines a robot, controller, task modules, and operator software.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MalocherBot is a modular industrial automation cell that combines a robot, controller, task modules, and operator software.

![MalocherBot palletizing cell with robot and pallet stations](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-malocherbot.webp)
*MalocherBot palletizing cell with robot and pallet stations. Source: [Unchained Robotics](https://unchainedrobotics.de/en/products/turnkey-solutions/unchained-robotics-malocherbot-palettieren), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Think beyond the arm:** Unchained Robotics packages the surrounding equipment into a usable production station rather than selling only a moving mechanism.
- **A concrete task is palletizing:** the robot takes boxes and builds a planned stack on a shipping pallet.
- **Software analogy:** its Base Unit resembles a server with plug-in services; LUNA connects the robot and selected task modules behind one interface.

> **Key idea:** A useful industrial robot is a coordinated system, not just an arm with a successful motion demo.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **The Base Unit contains** the robot, robot controller, system computer, and LUNA software.
- **Palletizer modules attach** to the Base Unit, which recognizes and configures them; the operator supplies box dimensions, weights, and stack patterns.
- **Worked calculation:** the advertised ceiling of 12 packages per minute corresponds to 60 ÷ 12 = 5 seconds per package, not guaranteed production performance.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Example configuration** | MalocherBot Palletizing |
| **Maximum box weight** | 20 kg |
| **Advertised maximum rate** | 12 packages/minute |
| **Maximum stack height** | 1.8 m |
| **Palletizer modules** | 1 or 2 |

## Key terms

- **Cell**: a robot and the surrounding equipment that perform one production task.
- **Palletizing**: arranging packages in layers on a pallet.
- **Turnkey**: supplied as an integrated solution rather than separate components.
- **Controller**: the computer responsible for executing robot motion.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the maker’s cell video and identify the Base Unit and pallet positions.
2. **Write a mock job description:** box dimensions, mass, pallet pattern, and what should happen when a pallet is full.
3. **Request a configured quote** before planning hardware access; the complete student deployment cost is unknown.

## Used in

- **Builder: Unchained Robotics.** compare the machine-tending and picking variants to see how the same integration idea serves different processes.
- **Study the boundaries:** a working box-stacking example does not automatically solve arbitrary-object grasping.

lessons.name: MORFOSE
lessons.summary: MORFOSE is a modular industrial robot whose rotating modules can be rearranged to suit different manufacturing tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MORFOSE is a modular industrial robot whose rotating modules can be rearranged to suit different manufacturing tasks.

![MORFOSE rotating modules and tool flange](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-morfose.webp)
*MORFOSE rotating modules and tool flange. Source: [MS-Innov](https://www.ms-innov.fr/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/COMMERCIAL_BOOKLET_MORFOSE.pdf), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Mechanics changes the program:** rebuilding the arm changes where its tool can move, not merely its appearance.
- **MS-Innov developed MORFOSE:** the manufacturer presents handling, assembly, inspection, and material-processing uses.
- **Software analogy:** reusable modules resemble software components, but their arrangement changes the physical geometry that the motion controller must understand.

> **Key idea:** Mechanical modularity is useful only when the controller and task configuration agree with the actual assembled robot.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Reconfigurable connections** let an operator replace modules or change the arm arrangement.
- **Unlimited axis rotation** means the published design has no rotational end stop on each module; it does not mean unlimited load capacity.
- **MARCUS software** provides graphical programming; the brochure also describes remotely synchronized modules for equipment such as turntables.
- **Worked comparison:** a six-axis arm plus a two-axis positioner has six arm axes, not eight axes inside the arm.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Maker’s product-page payload** | Up to 11 kg |
| **Reach** | Up to 1,200 mm |
| **Repeatability** | 0.1 mm |
| **Protection rating** | IP54 |
| **Module replacement/reconfiguration** | Under 10 minutes, maker claim |

## Key terms

- **Axis**: one independently controlled movement.
- **Positioner**: a separate mechanism that turns or positions the workpiece.
- **Repeatability**: how consistently the robot returns to a previously taught position.
- **Reconfiguration**: changing the physical arrangement of modules.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the product demonstration and mark which motion belongs to the arm versus external equipment.
2. **Compare sources:** the older brochure advertises up to 27 kg; use the configuration-specific product page rather than mixing those limits.
3. **Sketch one handling task** and request the matching configuration and quote; its current cost is unknown.

## Used in

- **MS-Innov is the map connection:** this robot illustrates its modular approach to industrial automation.
- **Compare with fixed arms:** ask which setup changes require rebuilding hardware and which require only editing the task.

lessons.name: MOTOMAN HC10DTP
lessons.summary: The MOTOMAN HC10DTP is a six-axis collaborative industrial arm with a 10 kg rated payload and hand-guided teaching.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The MOTOMAN HC10DTP is a six-axis collaborative industrial arm with a 10 kg rated payload and hand-guided teaching.

![MOTOMAN HC10DTP articulated collaborative robot](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-motoman-hc10dtp.webp)
*MOTOMAN HC10DTP articulated collaborative robot. Source: [Yaskawa](https://www.yaskawa.eu.com/robotics/robots/collaborative/productdetail/product/hc10dtp_17024), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Industrial scale is tangible:** this is production equipment for handling, not a small desktop learning kit.
- **Yaskawa Electric offers hand guidance:** an operator moves the wrist to teach positions, then the controller replays the programmed task.
- **Software analogy:** teaching points resembles recording function arguments; the controller executes the motion, but tools and surroundings still determine whether the task succeeds.

> **Key idea:** A collaborative arm’s force monitoring is one part of application safety, not permission to ignore the gripper or workpiece.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Six driven axes** position and orient the tool; supply cables are routed through the arm to the wrist.
- **Joint torque sensors** monitor twisting forces, supporting collision detection and the manufacturer’s stop and release functions.
- **Worked reach comparison:** the published absolute reach is 1,379 mm, while effective reach is 1,200 mm; these use different reference points.
- **Direct Teach buttons** save positions at the wrist; either the standard teach pendant or Smart Pendant can also program the robot.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Axes** | 6 |
| **Rated payload** | 10 kg |
| **Absolute reach** | 1,379 mm |
| **Effective reach** | 1,200 mm |
| **Repeatability** | 0.05 mm |
| **Robot weight** | 58 kg |
| **Power supply rating** | 1 kVA |

> **Watch out:** Moving arms, tools, and packages can trap or strike people; collaborative settings must match the complete application.

## Key terms

- **Payload**: the supported load at the tool, subject to the maker’s load conditions.
- **Torque sensor**: a sensor measuring twisting force at a joint.
- **Teach pendant**: a handheld interface for configuring and programming motion.
- **Effective reach**: the reach defined using the maker’s specified working reference points.

## Getting started

1. **Start free with the demonstration:** identify the tool and material flow before examining programming.
2. **Draw a pick-and-place cell:** include approach positions, pallet or fixture, and an explicit stopped state.
3. **Arrange a supplier demonstration:** price and complete cell cost are unknown; do not test contact behavior with your body.

## Used in

- **Yaskawa Electric is the builder:** compare the HC family’s reach and payload before choosing equipment.
- **Application examples matter:** a palletizer adds gripping, package presentation, and stacking logic beyond the arm specification.

lessons.name: NB-120
lessons.summary: NB-120 is Nimbl’Bot’s modular industrial arm prototype for operations such as machining, with many controllable bending sections.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

NB-120 is Nimbl’Bot’s modular industrial arm prototype for operations such as machining, with many controllable bending sections.

![NB-120 prototype with repeated metal modules](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-nb-120.webp)
*NB-120 prototype with repeated metal modules. Source: [Nimbl’Bot](https://nimbl-bot.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Flyer-corporate_Nimbl-Bot_ENG_2022_OK-web.pdf), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Its shape differs from a familiar elbow arm:** repeated modules bend along the length rather than concentrating motion at a few large joints.
- **Nimbl'Bot documents work with CEA:** the use case investigates machining complex materials after unsuitable tests with conventional solutions.
- **Software analogy:** commanding the tool is like specifying an API result while a solver chooses internal module states to produce it.

> **Key idea:** A prototype specification describes a particular configuration; it is not a promise that every modular assembly has the same capabilities.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **The 2022 flyer describes** a steel NB-120 prototype suitable for drilling, routing, and sanding.
- **A hollow structure** provides internal passage for services such as pipes; the flyer shows passages for pipes up to 8 mm diameter.
- **The CEA example** combines a spindle, meaning a rotating machining tool drive, with a CNC interface that accepts G-code motion instructions.
- **Worked comparison:** the flyer’s ten-module example is 2 m long; the current homepage lists a 1,000 mm configuration. Do not merge them.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Historical flyer configuration** | 10 modules |
| **Historical length** | 2 m |
| **Historical payload** | 10 kg |
| **Diameter** | 120 mm |
| **CEA prototype spindle** | 1.5 kW |
| **CEA example workspace** | 1 × 1 × 1 m |

> **Watch out:** A machining spindle introduces cutting and ejected-material hazards beyond those of moving the arm.

## Key terms

- **Module**: a repeatable mechanical unit in the arm.
- **Redundancy**: having more internal motion choices than a tool task alone requires.
- **G-code**: instructions describing manufacturing-machine movements.
- **Spindle**: the rotating drive carrying a machining tool.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the maker’s NB-120 simulation and separate simulated motion from demonstrated hardware performance.
2. **Read the flyer and CEA page together:** label each number with its source and configuration.
3. **Draft a tool-path experiment** without cutting material; current purchase access, supported software, and price are unknown.

## Used in

- **Nimbl'Bot is the builder:** its NB-55 targets narrower inspection environments rather than simply being the same arm at another scale.
- **CEA machining is the documented use case:** treat it as development evidence, not a general accuracy benchmark.

lessons.name: NB-55
lessons.summary: NB-55 is Nimbl’Bot’s slender modular arm for inspection and intervention in confined spaces.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

NB-55 is Nimbl’Bot’s slender modular arm for inspection and intervention in confined spaces.

![NB-55 prototype bent into a tight curve](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-nb-55.webp)
*NB-55 prototype bent into a tight curve. Source: [Nimbl’Bot](https://nimbl-bot.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Flyer-corporate_Nimbl-Bot_ENG_2022_OK-web.pdf), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Access is the central problem:** the robot is intended to reach areas that are difficult or risky for a person to inspect.
- **The maker describes rover mounting:** mobility brings the arm to the site, while the arm threads the tool into the inspection area.
- **Software analogy:** tool-path planning resembles routing around obstacles, except the entire physical arm must fit, not just its endpoint.

> **Key idea:** Reaching the target is insufficient if an intermediate arm section collides with the environment.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Repeated bending modules** make a snake-like shape; a hollow interior can carry communication cables and a 12 V supply in the historical design.
- **The 2022 flyer** lists NB-55 as a functional prototype for inspection and intervention, with a 60 mm diameter and 10 cm bending radius.
- **Configuration matters:** the same flyer describes an 80 cm prototype and a separate ten-module example measuring 60 cm.
- **Worked comparison:** that ten-module example has a stated 300° working area; it does not imply every point along a pipe is reachable.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **2022 prototype diameter** | 60 mm |
| **2022 listed length** | 80 cm |
| **2022 bending radius** | 10 cm |
| **2022 payload capacity** | 1 kg |
| **Ten-module example length** | 60 cm |
| **Ten-module working area** | 300° |

## Key terms

- **Bending radius**: the radius of the curve a bending section makes.
- **Confined space**: a restricted environment with limited room for access and movement.
- **Rover**: a mobile base carrying equipment.
- **Tool path**: the sequence of positions followed by the working end.

## Getting started

1. **Start free with the agility video:** track both the tip and the middle sections as the arm moves.
2. **Compare the dated flyer with the homepage:** the latter introduces NB K7-60 as a newer generation; do not copy its specifications into NB-55.
3. **Sketch a pipe-inspection scene** and identify pinch points and cable routing; present access and cost are unknown.

## Used in

- **Nimbl'Bot is the map connection:** NB-55 illustrates inspection-oriented manipulation.
- **Contrast NB-120:** the larger machining prototype solves a different tooling problem, even though both use modular construction.

lessons.name: Ned2
lessons.summary: Ned2 is Niryo’s six-axis desktop robot arm for learning programming and small-object manipulation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Ned2 is Niryo’s six-axis desktop robot arm for learning programming and small-object manipulation.

![Ned2 desktop educational robot in a teaching setup](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-ned2.webp)
*Ned2 desktop educational robot in a teaching setup. Source: [Niryo](https://niryo.com/6-axis-educative-robot-ned2/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A complete teaching platform** lets software students study moving hardware without first designing an arm.
- **Niryo offers graphical and code-based programming:** its technical sheet lists Niryo Studio, the Niryo API, and ROS.
- **Software analogy:** a robot API turns a desired operation into physical effects; unlike a pure function, a failed grasp changes the next input scene.

> **Key idea:** A repeatable arm still needs correctly placed objects, a suitable tool, and a task that fits its small payload.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Six rotating joints** position and orient the end tool; the structure uses aluminum, ABS plastic, and steel.
- **Digital and analog connections** link peripherals, while dedicated interfaces support a gripper, vacuum pump, and conveyor.
- **The 2025 technical sheet** specifies 300 g payload at its stated 20 mm tool-center condition; load placement therefore matters.
- **Worked calculation:** 300 g equals 0.3 kg, so this is a small-object platform rather than an industrial carton-handling arm.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Rotating joints** | 6 |
| **Robot mass** | 7 kg |
| **Payload** | 300 g, specified at z = 20 mm TCP |
| **Reach** | 490 mm |
| **Repeatability** | ±0.5 mm, ISO 9283 |
| **Average standard-use power** | 20 W |

## Key terms

- **TCP**: tool center point: the reference point used to describe tool motion.
- **Repeatability**: consistency when returning to the same commanded position.
- **Peripheral**: an attached device such as a gripper or conveyor.
- **API**: a documented interface through which a program requests robot operations.

## Getting started

1. **Start free with Niryo Academy:** follow the Ned2 getting-started course and identify the robot’s basic controls.
2. **On an available arm,** begin with the official setup and calibration workflow before a simple empty-gripper movement.
3. **Build a small pick-and-place exercise** with known object positions; purchase price and complete classroom setup cost are unknown.

## Used in

- **Niryo is the builder:** Ned2 is its educational arm in this map.
- **Read the stack’s version labels:** the linked documentation explicitly covers Ned2 and Ned3pro, so select the Ned2 instructions rather than assuming identical hardware.

lessons.name: OMX
lessons.summary: OMX is ROBOTIS’s lightweight leader–follower arm platform for teleoperation and imitation-learning experiments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

OMX is ROBOTIS’s lightweight leader–follower arm platform for teleoperation and imitation-learning experiments.

![OMX leader–follower manipulation hardware](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-omx.webp)
*OMX leader–follower manipulation hardware. Source: [ROBOTIS](https://ai.robotis.com/omx/hardware_omx.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Demonstrations become data:** move the leader and the follower performs the corresponding motion.
- **ROBOTIS uses DYNAMIXEL-X actuators** and ROS 2 workflows, with documented integration into LeRobot.
- **Software analogy:** the leader is an input device, while the follower is a physical output device; recording both makes a dataset rather than just a remote-control session.

> **Key idea:** A leader–follower system produces useful training data only when its physical setup and recorded observations agree.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **OMX-L is the leader:** its lightweight mechanism provides the human input; OMX-F is the powered follower.
- **Each has five arm joints plus a gripper:** the gripper’s opening is not an extra arm-orientation axis.
- **Follower load depends on reach:** the maker lists 100 g at full extension and 250 g at normal reach.
- **Worked calculation:** 250 ÷ 100 = 2.5; the normal-reach payload is 2.5 times the full-reach figure, not a universal lifting limit.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Arm layout** | 5 joints + gripper per unit |
| **Follower reach** | 400 mm |
| **Follower mass** | 560 g |
| **Follower supply** | 12 VDC |
| **Leader supply** | 5 VDC |
| **Full-reach payload** | 100 g |
| **Normal-reach payload** | 250 g |

## Key terms

- **Leader**: the mechanism a person moves to issue commands.
- **Follower**: the robot executing those commands.
- **Imitation learning**: learning robot behavior from recorded demonstrations.
- **Homing**: moving into the documented reference state before operation.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the OMX introduction and read the cable and setup instructions.
2. **Check the two supply voltages** and connect each unit exactly as the maker specifies; kit cost is unknown.
3. **Follow setup and operation guides** before collecting a simple object-transfer demonstration.

## Used in

- **ROBOTIS builds OMX:** its documented LeRobot workflow makes it a comparison platform for SO-101.
- **Keep evaluation separate from teaching:** record demonstrations first, then test whether a learned behavior works on new object placements.

lessons.name: OMY
lessons.summary: OMY is ROBOTIS’s six-joint manipulator family for teleoperation, learned manipulation, and research automation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

OMY is ROBOTIS’s six-joint manipulator family for teleoperation, learned manipulation, and research automation.

![OMY leader–follower manipulation hardware](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-omy.webp)
*OMY leader–follower manipulation hardware. Source: [ROBOTIS](https://ai.robotis.com/omy/hardware_omy.html), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Human demonstrations connect code to motion:** the OMY-AI3M set pairs an OMY-L100 leader with an OMY-F3M follower.
- **ROBOTIS documents the complete system:** the follower includes a two-finger hand and an Intel RealSense D405 depth camera.
- **Software analogy:** a demonstration is a logged input/output trace; training uses many traces to produce a policy that chooses later robot actions.

> **Key idea:** A leader–follower system produces useful training data only when its physical setup and recorded observations agree.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **DYNAMIXEL-Y actuators** drive six follower joints; Ethernet connects the host and RS485 carries internal communication.
- **The camera supplies depth observations,** while the hand supplies physical contact; neither alone completes a manipulation task.
- **Six degrees of freedom** describe arm motion, not six independent fingers or autonomous capabilities.
- **Worked comparison:** 580 mm reach is 0.58 m; the 3 kg payload specification does not make OMY a large-pallet robot.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Follower model** | OMY-F3M |
| **Arm degrees of freedom** | 6 |
| **Payload** | 3 kg |
| **Reach** | 580 mm |
| **Follower mass** | 13.5 kg |
| **Supply** | 24 VDC |
| **Repeatability** | ±0.05 mm |

## Key terms

- **Degree of freedom**: an independently controlled movement.
- **Depth camera**: a camera that also estimates distance to visible surfaces.
- **Policy**: a function mapping observations to chosen actions.
- **Inference**: running a trained model to produce outputs.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the OMY introduction and compare the available leader and follower configurations.
2. **Read the official setup guide:** confirm the host connection, supplied power equipment, and emergency stop before operation.
3. **Plan a demonstration dataset** for one small-object task; hardware pricing and complete experiment cost are unknown.

## Used in

- **ROBOTIS is the builder:** OMY is a larger research platform than OMX, not merely another name for it.
- **Its documented learning workflow** supports collecting demonstrations and later running models; owning the arm does not itself provide a trained task policy.

lessons.summary: P-Rob is F&P Robotics’ family of collaborative arms; P-Rob Eco is a concrete variant for light handling and automation.

## In one sentence

P-Rob is F&P Robotics’ family of collaborative arms; P-Rob Eco is a concrete variant for light handling and automation.

![P-Rob Eco collaborative robot arm](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-p-rob.webp)
*P-Rob Eco collaborative robot arm. Source: [F&P Robotics](https://www.fp-robotics.com/solutions/cobots/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A named family is not one specification:** choose a particular P-Rob variant before comparing payload or reach.
- **BFH HuCE Robotics Laboratory lists F&P P-Rob** in its robot park, giving this map node a concrete research connection.
- **Software analogy:** an arm is a hardware backend; the task software still needs adapters for the gripper, camera, and surrounding instruments.

> **Key idea:** Compare a complete variant and its integration interfaces, not specifications collected from different generations of the same robot family.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **P-Rob Eco uses six axes:** the vendor listing describes collision detection, a web-based interface, and a compact collaborative arm.
- **The controller executes motion,** while a chosen end tool determines whether the system grips a sample, carries an item, or operates a fixture.
- **The manufacturer’s application page** discusses laboratory handling, electronic testing, and bottle filling rather than claiming one universal task.
- **Worked planning example:** list sample pickup, instrument loading, and return as separate operations; give each an explicit success or failure outcome.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Illustrated variant** | P-Rob Eco |
| **Arm axes** | 6 |
| **Variant payload** | 5 kg |
| **Variant reach** | 900 mm |
| **Programming interface** | myP software / web interface |

## Key terms

- **Cobot**: a robot designed to support collaborative applications, with application-specific safety requirements.
- **End tool**: the device attached to the arm for the actual task.
- **Integration**: connecting the arm, tools, sensing, and task software.
- **Variant**: a particular model within a broader product family.

## Getting started

1. **Begin free:** watch the P-Rob Eco demonstration and identify its arm and gripper.
2. **Inspect the Eco listing** rather than transferring numbers from another P-Rob generation; current complete-system cost is unknown.
3. **Ask BFH about appropriate access:** its equipment-leasing statement concerns SMEs, not automatic student access.

## Used in

- **F&P Robotics is the builder:** the official cobot page provides industrial and laboratory application context.
- **BFH HuCE Robotics Laboratory is the mapped user:** treat that as evidence of a research platform, not proof of an open student hardware program.

lessons.name: P3020
lessons.summary: P3020 is Doosan Robotics’ five-axis collaborative arm for lifting heavy goods and stacking them on pallets.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

P3020 is Doosan Robotics’ five-axis collaborative arm for lifting heavy goods and stacking them on pallets.

![Navy P3020 industrial arm with its base and articulated joints](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-p3020.webp)
*Navy P3020 industrial arm with its base and articulated joints. Source: [Doosan Robotics](https://www.doosanrobotics.com/en/product-solutions/product/p-series/p3020/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Palletizing means stacking goods** on a transport platform, not solving arbitrary household manipulation.
- **Software analogy:** think of a packing service whose output is a physical stack; motion is only one part of delivering each request.
- **A narrow task shapes hardware:** Doosan chose five axes for palletizing rather than maximizing the arm’s possible movements.

> **Key idea:** Choose the robot around the task’s load and geometry, not around the most impressive demonstration.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **The arm moves the load:** its five-axis structure is optimized for palletizing.
- **The controller connects peripherals:** surrounding automation equipment must coordinate with robot movement.
- **The teach pendant supplies commands:** this tablet-like interface supports programming and application configuration.
- **Worked conversion:** 2,030 mm ÷ 1,000 = 2.03 m of reach; that is not a promise of reaching every point in a warehouse.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Axes** | 5 |
| **Payload** | 30 kg |
| **Reach** | 2,030 mm |
| **Repeatability** | ±0.1 mm |
| **Announced** | May 2024 |

## Key terms

- **Payload**: the maximum supported load, not the robot’s own weight.
- **Reach**: how far the arm can extend from its base.
- **Repeatability**: how consistently it returns to a previously commanded position.
- **Pallet**: a platform used to transport a stack of goods.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the PalletizHD demonstration and list the equipment surrounding the P3020.
2. **Sketch a mock task:** identify the pickup position, pallet position, and desired box layers before considering motion code.
3. **Ask for a configured quote:** current purchase and complete cell costs are unknown here; do not budget only for the arm.

> **Watch out:** Heavy loads and moving mechanisms create crushing hazards; a collaborative label is not a complete cell safety assessment.

## Used in

- **Builder: Doosan Robotics.** ONExia’s 2024 exhibition report identifies P3020 as the arm in its PalletizHD system.
- **Study task integration:** compare the arm’s specifications with the complete packaging station rather than treating them as interchangeable products.

lessons.name: Poppy Ergo Jr
lessons.summary: Poppy Ergo Jr is an open-source, six-degree-of-freedom educational arm made from printable parts, XL-320 motors, and a Raspberry Pi.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Poppy Ergo Jr is an open-source, six-degree-of-freedom educational arm made from printable parts, XL-320 motors, and a Raspberry Pi.

![Poppy Ergo Jr showing interchangeable tool configurations](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-poppy-ergo-jr.webp)
*Poppy Ergo Jr showing interchangeable tool configurations. Source: [Poppy Project](https://github.com/poppy-project/poppy-ergo-jr), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **The design is inspectable:** the repository exposes mechanical parts and software rather than hiding the robot behind a product video.
- **Small building blocks teach integration:** printed links, motors, and a controller turn abstract commands into visible movement.
- **Software analogy:** interchangeable tools resemble plug-ins; the arm stays recognizable while its application changes from holding a pen to grasping.

> **Key idea:** An open design lets you study the connection between code and mechanism, but old setup instructions still need compatibility checks.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Printed shapes form the structure:** the repository describes parts printable with FDM, a method that deposits material layer by layer.
- **Dynamixel XL-320 motors move joints:** a Raspberry Pi runs the control software.
- **Three tools change the application:** the documented choices are a lampshade, grasper, and pen holder.
- **Worked inventory:** six joint coordinates require six values in a pose record; use that as a data-model exercise, not an executable motor command.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 6 |
| **Motor family** | Dynamixel XL-320 |
| **Documented controllers** | Raspberry Pi 2 or 3 |
| **Documented tools** | 3 |
| **Setup-script SD-card minimum** | 8 GB |

## Key terms

- **Degree of freedom**: an independent movement coordinate describing the mechanism.
- **End effector**: the tool attached at the working end of the arm.
- **Pose record**: stored values describing one robot configuration.
- **Digital twin**: a software representation connected to a physical system.

## Getting started

1. **Inspect free design files:** browse the hardware directory and identify the printed pieces before sourcing a kit; current kit cost is unknown.
2. **Compare available electronics** with the archived repository’s Raspberry Pi assumptions; do not blindly execute its historical installation script.
3. **Draft two pose records:** name six joint fields, then explain how changing the tool could change the task without changing those fields.
4. **Watch the digital-twin demonstration:** distinguish the physical arm from its on-screen representation before investigating the implementation.

## Used in

- **Builder: Poppy Project.** This platform is presented as an educational entry point into robot manipulation.
- **HARFANG’s demonstration** connects a Poppy Ergo Jr to a Python-based digital representation; it is a separate project, not proof of current kit support.

lessons.name: R-One+
lessons.summary: R-One+ is Robocath’s physician-controlled robot for remotely manipulating guidewires and balloon or stent catheters during coronary interventions.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

R-One+ is Robocath’s physician-controlled robot for remotely manipulating guidewires and balloon or stent catheters during coronary interventions.

![R-One+ medical robotic assistance equipment](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-r-one.webp)
*R-One+ medical robotic assistance equipment. Source: [Robocath](https://www.robocath.com/product/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Assistance is not autonomy:** a physician controls instruments from a command unit rather than delegating clinical decisions to software.
- **The working environment matters:** remote manipulation lets the physician sit behind radiation protection instead of standing beside the X-ray imaging equipment.
- **Software analogy:** separate command interface from execution backend; the joysticks request movement and the robotic unit handles the instruments.

> **Key idea:** The useful robot here is a precise instrument interface, not an autonomous doctor or a general-purpose grabbing arm.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Two units divide responsibilities:** the command unit serves the physician; the robotic unit includes an articulated support arm.
- **The guidewire joystick** commands forward/backward movement, rotation, or both together; the other joystick translates the stent/balloon catheter.
- **A disposable sterile cassette** holds the instrument paths; a clamp keeps the guidewire position fixed when required.
- **Worked interface example:** represent a guidewire request as translation plus rotation, but a catheter request as translation only, matching the documented joystick functions.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Core units** | 2 |
| **Guidewire joystick speeds** | 2 |
| **Catheter joystick speeds** | 2 |
| **Numbered instrument paths** | 3, including standby |
| **Cassette** | Sterile, disposable per procedure |

## Key terms

- **Guidewire**: a thin wire used to guide interventional instruments through blood vessels.
- **Catheter**: a slender tube introduced into the body for a medical procedure.
- **Translation**: movement forward or backward without describing rotation.
- **Stent**: a small supporting structure placed to help keep a vessel open.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch Robocath’s R-One+ product animation and identify the command and robotic units.
2. **Draw the command boundary:** list the documented joystick movements and distinguish the physician’s decisions from the robot’s mechanical actions.
3. **Request official information:** the maker supplies the user manual on request; hardware price and student access are unknown.

> **Watch out:** This is clinical equipment involving invasive instruments and X-rays, not hardware for unsupervised student experiments.

## Used in

- **Builder: Robocath.** Its product page describes robotic assistance in interventional cardiology, where physicians treat the heart’s blood vessels.
- **Study precise teleoperation:** the platform illustrates why instrument locking, sterile consumables, and returning to manual operation belong in the system design.

lessons.name: Schindler R.I.S.E
lessons.summary: Schindler R.I.S.E is a robotic elevator-installation system that drills shaft walls and sets anchor bolts before installers fit the remaining equipment.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Schindler R.I.S.E is a robotic elevator-installation system that drills shaft walls and sets anchor bolts before installers fit the remaining equipment.

![Schindler R.I.S.E working inside an elevator shaft, from its official video](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-schindler-rise.webp)
*Schindler R.I.S.E working inside an elevator shaft, from its official video. Source: [Schindler](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jtRWCL5xVCs), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **A repetitive construction task** becomes a concrete robotics problem: place anchors accurately inside a tall, narrow shaft.
- **Automation has a boundary:** drilling and setting anchors are not the same as installing an entire working elevator.
- **Software analogy:** the building model resembles an input specification; the robot executes physical operations and records results back into that model.

> **Key idea:** A narrow autonomous workflow can be valuable without replacing the whole construction process.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **An industrial robot rides a platform:** a winch moves the system vertically through the shaft; it braces against the walls before drilling.
- **A rebar sensor detects reinforcement:** steel inside concrete affects where drilling can happen.
- **Digital building data supplies positions:** an execution plan defines drilling locations, while a digital installation record documents the completed work.
- **Worked workload:** the 2024 Vienna example needed 942 holes and 942 anchor placements across two shafts: 942 × 2 = 1,884 operations of those types.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Transportation trolley wheels** | 4 |
| **Scanning tools** | 2: surface and reinforcement |
| **Vienna example shaft height** | 100 m |
| **Vienna example shafts** | 2 |
| **Vienna example anchors** | 942 total |

## Key terms

- **Shaft**: the vertical space in which an elevator travels.
- **Anchor bolt**: a fastening installed into the structure to support attached equipment.
- **Rebar**: steel reinforcement embedded in concrete.
- **BIM**: Building Information Modeling, a digital representation used to coordinate building information.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the job-site report, noting its disclosed paid promotion for Schindler.
2. **Trace one anchor:** sketch the path from planned position through wall inspection, drilling, placement, and recorded result.
3. **Separate automated work** from the installers’ remaining responsibilities; actual deployment access and price are unknown, so begin with a workflow study.

> **Watch out:** Elevator shafts and industrial drilling are hazardous work environments; this lesson proposes analysis, not a physical shaft experiment.

## Used in

- **Builder: Schindler.** The B1M’s 2024 report follows its deployment at Vienna’s Schneewittchen tower.
- **On-site support remains:** the operator monitors cameras, manages consumables, and supports quality control even though the installation steps run independently.

lessons.name: PAL Robotics SEA arm (ICRA 2026)
lessons.summary: PAL Robotics’ ICRA 2026 SEA arm is a seven-degree-of-freedom research manipulator subsequently presented as TIAGo Pro Arm.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

PAL Robotics’ ICRA 2026 SEA arm is a seven-degree-of-freedom research manipulator subsequently presented as TIAGo Pro Arm.

![TIAGo Pro Arm standalone research manipulator](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-pal-sea-arm.webp)
*TIAGo Pro Arm standalone research manipulator. Source: [PAL Robotics](https://pal-robotics.com/robot/arm/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **The map uses a launch-era label:** PAL’s May announcement described the unnamed SEA platform; its September announcement names the standalone platform TIAGo Pro Arm.
- **Low-level access supports experiments:** ROS 2 software and direct control access let researchers investigate movement rather than only replay packaged demonstrations.
- **Software analogy:** a spring between actuator and load resembles a buffer that absorbs disturbances instead of transmitting every shock directly.

> **Key idea:** Mechanical flexibility and software access are complementary tools for studying manipulation, not guarantees that every interaction is safe.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Seven movement coordinates** give the arm flexibility in positioning its tool; a quick tool changer supports swapping end effectors.
- **Series Elastic Actuators contain elasticity:** PAL describes an elastic element that absorbs impacts, protecting hardware during experiments.
- **The base integrates electronics:** the launch announcement places the user panel and power board inside the base rather than a separate control box.
- **Worked timing:** 1 kHz means 1,000 control updates each second, or a nominal 1 ms interval; application software must respect that timing boundary.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Degrees of freedom** | 7 |
| **Low-level control rate** | 1 kHz |
| **Product-table mass** | 9.5 kg |
| **Product-table repeatability** | 0.3 mm |
| **Continuously rotating joints** | 1, 3, 5 |

## Key terms

- **Actuator**: the mechanism that converts supplied energy into movement.
- **Compliance**: the ability to yield under an applied force instead of remaining perfectly rigid.
- **Torque**: turning effort around a joint.
- **End effector**: the hand, gripper, or other tool attached to the arm.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch PAL’s TIAGo Pro introduction to see the related mobile robot and its arms, not a standalone-arm demonstration.
2. **Explore the product interface:** the documented browser WebGUI provides diagnostics, joint control, and visual programming for an available robot.
3. **Request a configuration and quote:** purchase cost is unknown here; confirm load and reach requirements because the product page contains conflicting figures.

## Used in

- **Builder: PAL Robotics.** Its September 2026 material targets manipulation, robot learning, and perception research using the standalone arm.
- **Check integration boundaries:** PAL describes mounting it alone or integrating it with mobile platforms; mobility and manipulation remain separate capabilities to coordinate.

lessons.name: Sepro 3-axis injection-molding robots
lessons.summary: Sepro’s three-axis robots move molded plastic parts out of injection-molding machines and into downstream handling operations.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Sepro’s three-axis robots move molded plastic parts out of injection-molding machines and into downstream handling operations.

![Sepro S-Line Cartesian robot with its overhead beam and vertical arm](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-sepro-3-axis.webp)
*Sepro S-Line Cartesian robot with its overhead beam and vertical arm. Source: [Sepro Group](https://www.sepro-group.com/press-room/new-s-line-high-performance-robots-from-sepro-deliver-higher-speeds-longer-strokes-more-payload), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Task-specific hardware:** injection molding shapes plastic inside a mold; the robot removes the finished part rather than manufacturing the plastic itself.
- **Software analogy:** a Cartesian robot resembles moving a cursor through three coordinates, rather than coordinating a human-shaped arm.
- **A family, not one model:** this map node covers Sepro’s three-axis machines; the redesigned S-Line is a concrete, documented example introduced in 2025.

> **Key idea:** A constrained movement pattern can simplify automation when the same extraction task repeats every production cycle.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Linear motion:** an overhead beam and vertical arm position the gripping tool around the molding machine.
- **Servo drives:** controlled motors move the three axes; Visual 4 provides the S-Line’s control interface.
- **Configuration matters:** S-Line can also add wrist rotations for five-axis motion; that option is not the basic three-axis configuration.
- **Spec example:** the current S-Line page lists these S-15 values; they are not specifications for every Sepro robot.

| Specification | S-15 example |
| --- | --- |
| **Basic controlled axes** | 3 |
| **Molding-machine clamping force** | 100–300 metric tons |
| **Maximum load, parts plus tool** | 6 kg |
| **Vertical stroke options** | 1,000 / 1,200 / 1,400 mm |
| **Standard ejector stroke** | 500 mm |

- **Worked load budget:** with an illustrative 2 kg tool, a 6 kg combined limit leaves 6 − 2 = 4 kg for parts.

## Key terms

- **Cartesian robot**: a mechanism organized around straight-line coordinate movements.
- **Stroke**: the available travel along one movement direction.
- **End effector**: the gripping tool at the robot’s working end.
- **Clamping force**: the molding machine’s force holding the mold closed, not the robot’s lifting capacity.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch Sepro’s S-Line introduction and identify the beam, vertical arm, and part-handling tool.
2. **Model a cycle:** write a paper state machine for waiting, extracting, transferring, and returning; do not connect it to machinery.
3. **Check the configuration:** request a supplier quote for the actual molding machine and tool; purchase price is unknown here.

> **Watch out:** Mold closing and robot travel create crushing hazards; extraction must be coordinated with the machine’s safety system.

## Used in

- **Builder: Sepro Group.** Its documented applications include automotive, packaging, and medical molding automation.
- **Compare SSI Piece Picking:** both move parts, but warehouse picking must choose items from changing arrangements rather than follow one mold-extraction cycle.

lessons.name: SSI Piece Picking
lessons.summary: SSI Piece Picking is a robotic warehouse cell that recognizes, grips, verifies, and places individual products into order containers.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

SSI Piece Picking is a robotic warehouse cell that recognizes, grips, verifies, and places individual products into order containers.

![SSI Piece Picking robotic cell handling products between containers](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-ssi-piece-picking.webp)
*SSI Piece Picking robotic cell handling products between containers. Source: [SSI SCHAEFER](https://www.ssi-schaefer.com/en-us/products/picking-handling/automated-picking/piece-picking-1085472), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Picking connects perception to records:** moving an object is not enough; the warehouse must know which item moved and whether the quantity is correct.
- **Software analogy:** think of a checked database transaction: identify the requested record, perform the transfer, then verify the result before accepting it.
- **Product differences matter:** suction tools and placement strategies must cope with changing packaging, not just repeat one fixed arm movement.

> **Key idea:** Reliable picking includes identification and verification, not merely a successful-looking grasp.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Object recognition:** camera-based AI identifies products and selects where the tool should grip them.
- **Compact suction cups:** these reach into containers and lift products; gentle placement reduces damage compared with dropping items.
- **Scanning and weighing:** barcode reading checks identity, while weight helps verify the picked quantity.
- **WAMAS software:** coordinates material flow and vision integration, connecting the cell to warehouse management.
- **Manufacturer figures:** the launch article gives these conditional performance claims, not guaranteed results for every product assortment.

| Specification or benchmark | Published value |
| --- | --- |
| **Maximum picking rate** | Up to 1,200 individual pieces/hour |
| **First-attempt barcode reading** | At least 99.5% of products |
| **Reported pharmaceutical coverage** | 80% of product spectrum |
| **Verification target** | 100% product verification through scanning and weighing |

- **Worked ideal rate:** 3,600 seconds ÷ 1,200 pieces = 3 seconds per piece; difficult products and interruptions change real throughput.

## Key terms

- **Pick-and-place**: moving an item to a chosen destination position rather than simply releasing it.
- **Gripping point**: the selected contact location between tool and product.
- **Barcode**: a machine-readable product identifier printed on packaging.
- **WMS**: warehouse management system, software tracking inventory and orders.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the official demonstration and separate recognition, gripping, placement, and verification into distinct stages.
2. **Build a mock transaction:** use product IDs and expected weights in a local program; reject missing scans instead of silently counting success.
3. **Study deployment needs:** request a configured supplier quote; the public sources do not establish a complete installed price.

## Used in

- **Builder: SSI Schäfer.** The manufacturer describes applications in e-commerce, retail, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and third-party logistics.
- **Compare Swisslog ItemPiQ:** both combine robot motion with perception and warehouse software; compare verification behavior rather than judging only video speed.

lessons.name: Swisslog ItemPiQ
lessons.summary: Swisslog ItemPiQ is a vision-guided robotic picking system that transfers individual products from source bins into order bins or cartons.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Swisslog ItemPiQ is a vision-guided robotic picking system that transfers individual products from source bins into order bins or cartons.

![Swisslog ItemPiQ robotic picking installation at LogiMAT](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-swisslog-itempiq.webp)
*Swisslog ItemPiQ robotic picking installation at LogiMAT. Source: [Swisslog](https://www.swisslog.com/en-us/products-systems-solutions/picking-palletizing-order-fulfillment/robotic-piece-picking-itempiq), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **An order becomes a physical action:** warehouse software requests an item, vision locates it, and a robot executes the transfer.
- **Software analogy:** the picking cell is like a worker consuming jobs from a queue; the surrounding warehouse system coordinates which job comes next.
- **Not one immutable arm:** ItemPiQ is a system offering that has evolved; its current brochure is more useful for sizing than older launch specifications.

> **Key idea:** A picking system succeeds when perception, gripping, and order-management software agree on the same physical transfer.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Intelligent vision:** recognizes items and selects a picking method, including for previously unknown products.
- **Adaptable tools:** the current product page describes autonomous gripper exchange and four automatically selected grasping methods.
- **Warehouse integration:** standard interfaces connect warehouse software; Swisslog also integrates the cell with its SynQ platform and AutoStore systems.
- **Brochure specifications:** these describe the published ItemPiQ offering, not every historical installation or achievable rate for every assortment.

| Specification | Brochure value |
| --- | --- |
| **Typical performance** | 600 items/hour |
| **Technical robot performance** | Up to 1,000 picks/hour |
| **Robot reach** | Over 1,100 mm |
| **Product payload** | Up to 3.0 kg |
| **Maximum product dimensions** | 300 × 300 × 300 mm |

- **Worked comparison:** 3,600 ÷ 600 = 6 seconds per item at the typical rate, versus 3.6 seconds at the technical maximum.
- **Interpretation:** those averages describe different performance measures; neither predicts an entire warehouse’s shipping output by itself.

## Key terms

- **Source bin**: the container holding products before selection.
- **Target bin**: the destination container receiving the selected item.
- **Grasping method**: the tool-contact strategy used to hold a product.
- **Throughput**: completed items per unit of time, measured across a stated process boundary.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the official demonstration and follow one item from source container to destination.
2. **Simulate a queue:** generate mock picking requests and compare completion times using six-second and 3.6-second service times; label these illustrative averages.
3. **Check real requirements:** use the brochure’s size and weight envelope before requesting a configured quote; installed price is unknown here.

## Used in

- **Builder: Swisslog.** The current page lists fashion, electronics, consumer goods, and food-and-beverage applications.
- **Compare TGW RovoFlex and SSI Piece Picking:** all integrate picking with warehouse operations, but their published figures describe different configurations and test conditions.

lessons.name: TGW RovoFlex
lessons.summary: TGW RovoFlex is a camera-guided picking robot that can work in a PickCenter station with switchable automatic and manual operating modes.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TGW RovoFlex is a camera-guided picking robot that can work in a PickCenter station with switchable automatic and manual operating modes.

![TGW RovoFlex articulated picking arm above warehouse containers](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-tgw-rovoflex.webp)
*TGW RovoFlex articulated picking arm above warehouse containers. Source: [TGW Logistics](https://www.tgw-group.com/en/news/detail/next-level-order-picking-with-rovoflex/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Automation is not all-or-nothing:** PickCenter RovoFlex supports changing between manual and automatic operation, useful when order demand changes.
- **Software analogy:** imagine a service with automatic processing and an operator-controlled mode; changing modes is part of the system design, not a failed demonstration.
- **Real integration matters:** TGW’s INTERSPORT case describes a RovoFlex-equipped PickCenter inside a larger automated fulfillment center.

> **Key idea:** Design the workstation around changing operating conditions, not just the robot’s fastest repeated motion.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Intelligent camera system:** observes goods so the robot can select and execute picking actions.
- **Learning software:** TGW describes continuous improvement from gripping operations; this is the manufacturer’s account, not an independently measured accuracy guarantee.
- **PickCenter station:** combines the robot with the surrounding picking workflow and supports switching between manual and automatic modes.
- **Beyond one station:** the launch article also describes sorting, consolidation, and separation applications.
- **Source context:** the current product page and February 2024 launch give differently worded performance claims; do not silently merge them.

| Specification or configuration | Published value |
| --- | --- |
| **Launch year** | 2024 |
| **Current product-page throughput** | Up to 1,000 picks/hour |
| **Launch throughput claim** | Over 1,000 items/hour |
| **Operating modes** | 2: manual and automatic |
| **Other workstation layouts mentioned at launch** | 1:4 and 2:6 |

- **Worked ceiling:** 1,000 picks/hour × 0.5 hour = 500 picks at uninterrupted nominal pace; replenishment and interruptions reduce actual output.

## Key terms

- **Hybrid picking**: a workstation supporting both human-operated and automated picking modes.
- **Consolidation**: combining items into the group needed for a later operation or order.
- **Retrofit**: adding new equipment to an existing installation.
- **Fulfillment center**: a facility assembling and shipping customer orders.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the RovoFlex-specific official video and identify the robot, containers, and surrounding workstation.
2. **Sketch mode transitions:** model automatic, manual, and stopped states on paper; distinguish a mode request from permission to move.
3. **Read the deployment case:** list what the wider warehouse supplies to the station; request a supplier quote because installed cost is unknown here.

## Used in

- **Builder: TGW Logistics.** Its INTERSPORT release documents one PickCenter equipped with RovoFlex.
- **Compare Swisslog ItemPiQ:** both connect item handling to warehouse software, while RovoFlex explicitly highlights the manual/automatic workstation pattern.

lessons.name: TMS-Cobot
lessons.summary: TMS-Cobot is Axilum Robotics’ medical positioning robot that maintains a compatible magnetic-stimulation coil’s position, orientation, and contact as the patient’s head moves.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TMS-Cobot is Axilum Robotics’ medical positioning robot that maintains a compatible magnetic-stimulation coil’s position, orientation, and contact as the patient’s head moves.

![TMS-Cobot arm positioning a stimulation coil beside a seated patient](/img/lessons/robots_arm_2-tms-cobot.webp)
*TMS-Cobot arm positioning a stimulation coil beside a seated patient. Source: [Axilum Robotics](https://www.axilumrobotics.com/en/tms-cobot-features/), license unknown.*

## Why it matters for us

- **Positioning is the robot’s job:** TMS means transcranial magnetic stimulation; the compatible stimulator supplies the stimulation, while the robot handles the coil.
- **Software analogy:** a feedback controller resembles a continuously updated synchronization process, correcting a stored target when the tracked reference moves.
- **Human movement changes the problem:** a stationary coil holder cannot compensate for head motion the way a tracked robotic positioner can.

> **Key idea:** Maintaining a tool relative to a moving person requires tracking and contact feedback, not just replaying a fixed arm pose.

## What it is made of / how it works

- **Optical tracking:** cameras follow markers on the head, providing motion information to maintain coil position and orientation.
- **Pressure sensing:** an integrated sensor supports continued coil-to-head contact as motion compensation occurs.
- **Collaborative arm:** joint-level collision detection and a manual free-drive mode support positioning; compatible tracking or neuronavigation systems provide guidance.
- **Published hardware:** the features page reports the following arm accuracy and physical dimensions; arm accuracy is not a clinical-outcome guarantee.

| Specification | Manufacturer value |
| --- | --- |
| **Arm accuracy** | Below 2 mm |
| **Height with arm** | 1,770 mm |
| **Base dimensions** | 1,111 × 650 mm |
| **Weight** | 143 kg |

- **Worked conversion:** 1,111 mm ÷ 1,000 = 1.111 m; together with the 0.650 m base width, this helps sketch the cart footprint.

## Key terms

- **Coil**: the stimulation device component positioned near the head.
- **Neuronavigation**: guidance relating the coil’s position to a target using tracking and, where applicable, brain imaging.
- **Feedback**: measured information used to correct an ongoing action.
- **Free-drive**: a mode allowing the user to direct the arm manually.

## Getting started

1. **Start free:** watch the LOCALITE demonstration and distinguish the robot, coil, tracking system, and navigation display.
2. **Model tracking offline:** move a reference point in a toy program and update a target offset; this is not medical-control software.
3. **Read compatibility first:** clinical acquisition requires a compatible configuration; current purchase price is unknown here.

> **Watch out:** FDA clearance cited by Axilum specifically covers TMS-Cobot TS MV positioning the MagVenture therapy coil, not arbitrary stimulators or treatment protocols.

## Used in

- **Builder: Axilum Robotics.** Its page describes TMS-Cobot as a CE-marked class IIa device for its stated positioning use.
- **Keep products distinct:** neither that status nor the configuration-specific FDA statement should be generalized to the separate TMS-Robot or TUS-Cobot.
